events.text: Night settles over Blackhollow. Six strangers take their seats. Among them, two wolves wait.
The sun rises. Everyone survived the night.

A clean night gives us no corpse, not no information. Someone chose a target and someone prevented a death—or the wolves missed, which is less likely. Finn, why were you the apparent center of last night’s danger? I want your read first. Mara and Vera, don’t hide behind “no evidence”: name one player whose behavior you distrust and why.

Silas is manufacturing certainty from a blank dawn. Publicly, nothing identifies Finn as the attack target; survival could reflect a heal or an unmade attack, but neither centers Finn. That unsupported premise looks designed to force an early defensive reaction. Silas, what specific public event makes Finn the “apparent center” rather than any of the other five players?

Mara’s right that nothing public identifies Finn as the target. Silas, I’m willing to hear what led you there, but calling him the “apparent center” needs an explanation. Finn, I won’t treat your answer to an unsupported premise as evidence against you. Vera, would you help me judge Silas’s explanation on its merits rather than rush a vote?

Finn is cleared to me, so I’m not accepting Silas’s unsupported “center of danger” claim as a basis for pressure. Mara and Edgar correctly challenged the premise, while Silas has not supplied any concrete event behind it. My current hunch is that Silas is manufacturing a target; I want him to explain before I consider moving elsewhere.

Observed fact: everyone survived; nothing public identifies the target. I have no private information about an attack on me. Mara’s objection is sound, but Silas’s specificity could reflect private knowledge rather than fabrication. Iris’s clearance is also an unverified claim. I tentatively suspect Silas, not conclusively. Crucially, he has no second discussion turn, so his inability to answer now is not additional evidence.

Silas’s claim that Finn was the “apparent center” of danger has no support in the public record. That is my strongest reason to distrust his push, though, as Finn notes, Silas cannot answer again today. Iris, when you say Finn is “cleared to me,” are you offering evidence or a hunch? I won’t treat that confidence as a clearance without a basis.
Silas → Mara; Mara → Silas; Edgar → Silas; Iris → Silas; Finn → Silas; Vera → Silas
Silas is exiled from the village.
Night 2 falls. The village closes its eyes.
Did not survive the night: Iris.
The wolves prevail. Blackhollow belongs to the night.

replay.rules:
Six seats. Two Werewolves, one Seer, one Witch, and two Villagers.
Night: wolves choose a victim, the Seer investigates, then the Witch acts. Day: discussion, then a secret vote.
Wolves know their teammate and may leave a private message with their choice. If their targets differ, the referee randomly chooses one.
The Seer may investigate one other living player each night, learning only whether they are a wolf.
The Witch has one healing potion and one poison for the entire game. Only one potion may be used per night. Self-healing is allowed.
The Witch sees the attacked player only while the healing potion remains. Poison may target another living player.
Night actions resolve simultaneously. A player attacked that night may still use their ability. Death causes and identities stay hidden.
Each living player speaks once per day, then votes privately. Self-voting is forbidden; abstaining is allowed.
The unique highest-voted player is exiled. A tie or all abstentions means no exile. Individual votes are revealed after resolution.
The village wins when all wolves are eliminated. Wolves win when they equal or outnumber the remaining villagers, including special roles.
After six day-night cycles without a winner, the game is a draw. Eliminated players cannot act.
External players have 120 seconds per turn in autoplay. A timeout means silence, abstention, or skipping an ability.
Roles and private actions are revealed only when the game ends. Portraits and names are cosmetic, never clues to a role.
